title: Europe Struggles to Control Record-Breaking Wildfires Amid Extreme Heat
subtitle: As temperatures rise, firefighters across the continent face dangerous conditions and difficult battles to protect towns and forests.

summary.en: Southern Europe is facing a difficult summer as extreme heat fuels record-breaking wildfires. Thousands of people have been forced to leave their homes, and tragic losses have been reported among firefighting crews. While some evacuation orders in Spain have been lifted, officials remain on high alert. Scientists warn that climate change is making these fires more frequent and harder to control. European leaders are now calling for better preparation and new equipment to manage the growing crisis.
summary.zh: 南歐正經歷一個艱難的夏天，極端高溫助長了破紀錄的野火。數千人被迫撤離家園，救災團隊也傳出不幸的傷亡。儘管西班牙部分撤離令已解除，官員仍保持高度警戒。科學家警告，氣候變遷正使這些火災變得更頻繁且更難控制。歐洲領袖目前正呼籲加強準備工作並添購新設備，以應對日益嚴峻的危機。

paragraphs.en: Across southern Europe, countries are fighting some of the worst wildfires in their history. From the Atlantic coast to the Mediterranean, extreme heatwaves have turned forests and fields into dry, dangerous areas that catch fire easily. According to BBC Science & Environment, more than 300,000 people have been forced to leave their homes since the middle of July. The situation is particularly serious in France and Spain, where officials describe the fires as the most difficult they have ever faced.
paragraphs.zh: 南歐各國正與史上最嚴重的幾場野火搏鬥。從大西洋沿岸到地中海，極端熱浪已將森林與田野變成乾燥且危險的區域，極易引發火勢。根據英國廣播公司科學與環境頻道（BBC Science & Environment）報導，自七月中旬以來，已有超過三十萬人被迫撤離家園。法國與西班牙的情況尤為嚴峻，官員形容這些火災是他們面臨過最棘手的挑戰。

paragraphs.en: In France, the Gironde region near Bordeaux has been hit very hard. The fires there have burned an area roughly four times the size of Paris. The heat has been so intense that it created rare fire thunderstorms. These storms happen when hot air rises quickly, carrying smoke and ash high into the sky, which can sometimes create lightning and start even more fires. As reported by BBC Science & Environment, thousands of firefighters, police officers, and military personnel are working to stop the flames. Sadly, four French firefighters have died while on duty. Jean-Luc Gleyze, a local official, told the BBC that authorities do not have enough people or trucks to fight the fires effectively.
paragraphs.zh: 在法國，波爾多（Bordeaux）附近的吉倫特省（Gironde）受創最深。當地的火勢已燒毀面積約為巴黎四倍大的土地。高溫強烈到足以引發罕見的「火積雲雷雨」。當熱空氣迅速上升，將煙霧與灰燼帶往高空時，便會形成這種雷雨，有時甚至會產生閃電並引發更多火災。據 BBC 科學與環境頻道報導，數以千計的消防員、警察與軍事人員正努力撲滅火勢。令人遺憾的是，已有四名法國消防員在執勤時殉職。當地官員格萊茲（Jean-Luc Gleyze）向 BBC 表示，當局目前缺乏足夠的人力與消防車來有效控制火勢。

paragraphs.en: Spain is also dealing with its largest wildfire on record. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez recently visited a command center to oversee the response. According to The Guardian World, the prime minister said that the next 12 hours would be very important for controlling the fire. While the situation near the capital, Madrid, has shown some improvement, other areas remain dangerous. Deutsche Welle (DW) Top reports that Spanish authorities have started to lift some evacuation orders, allowing tens of thousands of people to return to their homes. However, many people returned only to find their houses and belongings destroyed by the flames.
paragraphs.zh: 西班牙也正處理該國有紀錄以來最大規模的野火。總理桑傑士（Pedro Sánchez）近日視察指揮中心以督導應變工作。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，總理表示接下來的十二小時對於控制火勢至關重要。雖然首都馬德里（Madrid）附近的狀況已有所改善，但其他地區依然危險。德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導指出，西班牙當局已開始解除部分撤離令，允許數萬名民眾返回家園。然而，許多人返家後卻發現房屋與財產已被烈火焚毀。

paragraphs.en: The human cost of these fires has been high. The Guardian World reports that three firefighters have died in Greece while trying to protect their communities. Across the continent, more than 120 firefighters have been injured in France alone. These brave crews are using planes to drop water and fire retardant—a special liquid used to slow down or stop the spread of fire—but the work is exhausting and dangerous. Strong winds and high temperatures often make the fires spread faster, forcing crews to change their plans constantly.
paragraphs.zh: 這些火災造成了慘重的人員傷亡。據《衛報》報導，希臘有三名消防員在保護社區時殉職。在整個歐洲大陸，僅法國一地就有超過一百二十名消防員受傷。這些英勇的救災人員利用飛機投放水與阻燃劑（一種用來減緩或阻止火勢蔓延的特殊液體），但這項工作既耗費體力又充滿危險。強風與高溫往往使火勢蔓延得更快，迫使救災團隊必須不斷調整策略。

paragraphs.en: Scientists say that these extreme events are becoming more common because of climate change. According to Deutsche Welle (DW) Top, carbon pollution is heating the European continent twice as fast as the global average. This makes summers hotter and drier, which dries out the land and creates perfect conditions for massive fires. Experts warn that because of these changes, fire seasons are lasting longer, and fires could potentially continue to burn well into November.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家指出，由於氣候變遷，這些極端事件正變得越來越頻繁。根據德國之聲報導，碳污染導致歐洲大陸的升溫速度是全球平均值的兩倍。這使得夏季變得更加炎熱乾燥，導致土地乾涸，為大規模野火創造了絕佳條件。專家警告，由於這些環境變化，野火季節正變得更長，火勢甚至可能持續燃燒至十一月。

paragraphs.en: Because the fires are becoming more extreme, European leaders are looking for new ways to respond. Currently, the European Union helps member countries by sharing resources when a fire becomes too big for one nation to handle alone. However, officials now believe that this is not enough. According to Deutsche Welle (DW) Top, the European Union is planning to buy its own permanent fleet of firefighting planes to be better prepared for the future. Hadja Lahbib, the EU's Crisis Management Commissioner, stated that because climate change is moving quickly, the response from European nations must also improve and grow faster.
paragraphs.zh: 由於火災日益極端，歐洲各國領袖正尋求新的應對方式。目前，歐盟（European Union）會在火勢大到單一國家無法獨自處理時，透過共享資源來協助成員國。然而，官員們現在認為這已不足夠。據德國之聲報導，歐盟計畫購買專屬的常設消防機隊，以便為未來做好更充分的準備。歐盟危機管理執委拉比（Hadja Lahbib）表示，由於氣候變遷進展迅速，歐洲各國的應對措施也必須加速改善與成長。

paragraphs.en: As the summer continues, the danger remains. While some people in Spain are finally able to go home, France is still facing high temperatures and warnings of more fire activity. Firefighters continue to patrol high-risk areas, watching for any sign of smoke. The combination of record-breaking heat and dry forests means that the risk of new fires is still very high. For now, the focus remains on protecting lives and keeping communities safe while hoping for cooler weather to help the exhausted crews finally bring the flames under control.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著夏季持續，危險依然存在。雖然西班牙部分民眾終於能夠返家，但法國仍面臨高溫與更多火災警報。消防員持續巡邏高風險區域，留意任何煙霧跡象。破紀錄的高溫加上乾燥的森林，意味著引發新火災的風險依然極高。目前，救災重點仍放在保護生命與維護社區安全，同時期盼氣溫下降，協助精疲力竭的救災人員最終能將火勢控制住。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be affected by something negative or harmful.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「打擊」的動作，這裡指地區受到災害影響。文中：In France, the Gironde region near Bordeaux has been hit very hard.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Known to have happened or existed; documented.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 有紀錄以來，史上記載的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 容易誤以為是「在唱片上」，實際上是指紀錄在案的。文中：Spain is also dealing with its largest wildfire on record.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To officially end a rule, law, or restriction.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「舉起」，這裡指解除撤離命令。文中：Spanish authorities have started to lift some evacuation orders, allowing tens of thousands of people to return to their homes.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Used to emphasize that something happens far into a period of time.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 遠遠地、深入地（用於強調時間）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「好地」，這裡用來強調時間持續到很晚。文中：Experts warn that because of these changes, fire seasons are lasting longer, and fires could potentially continue to burn well into November.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is a specific consequence of the intense heat in the Gironde region of France?

options.A: The destruction of four times the amount of land as the city of Paris.
options.B: The formation of unusual weather phenomena that can trigger further fires.
options.C: The immediate resignation of local officials due to a lack of resources.
options.D: The successful evacuation of all residents before the fire reached their homes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確提到，Gironde 地區的高溫產生了罕見的「火雷暴」（fire thunderstorms），這種現象會將煙霧和灰燼帶入高空，進而產生閃電並引發更多火災。選項 A 雖然提到了燃燒面積是巴黎的四倍，但這是火災的範圍而非「高溫導致的現象」。選項 C 錯誤，因為官員 Jean-Luc Gleyze 是抱怨資源不足，而非辭職。選項 D 文章並未提及所有居民都成功撤離，事實上許多人回家後發現家園已毀。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the current EU strategy for fighting wildfires be considered insufficient?

options.A: Because individual countries refuse to share their firefighting equipment with neighbors.
options.B: Because climate change is causing fires to occur in regions that have no firefighting infrastructure.
options.C: Because the speed and scale of climate-driven fires are outpacing the current resource-sharing model.
options.D: Because the EU has already spent its entire budget on purchasing private planes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，歐盟目前依賴成員國間的資源共享，但官員認為這已不足夠。結合第五段提到氣候變遷導致火災更頻繁、更嚴重，且第六段末尾提到氣候變遷移動速度很快，歐盟的應對必須更快，可推論出目前的資源共享模式已無法應付氣候變遷帶來的嚴峻挑戰。選項 A 與文章內容矛盾，因為歐盟確實有資源共享機制。選項 B 文章未提及無基礎設施的地區。選項 D 為過度推論，文章僅提到歐盟正計劃購買自己的機隊，而非預算用盡。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'retardant' refer to in the context of firefighting?

options.A: A chemical substance used to inhibit the progression of flames.
options.B: A type of aircraft designed to carry large amounts of water.
options.C: A protective suit worn by firefighters to endure high temperatures.
options.D: A strategy used to evacuate people from dangerous zones.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章第四段提到「fire retardant—a special liquid used to slow down or stop the spread of fire」，這明確定義了該詞是指一種用來減緩或阻止火勢蔓延的特殊化學液體。選項 B 錯誤，飛機是載具而非液體本身。選項 C 錯誤，這不是指消防員的個人防護裝備。選項 D 錯誤，這與撤離策略無關，而是針對火勢本身的控制手段。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the wildfires in Europe?

options.A: The wildfires are primarily caused by human error and poor urban planning in southern Europe.
options.B: Firefighters are successfully controlling most wildfires, but the economic cost is very high.
options.C: Climate change is intensifying wildfires, necessitating a more robust and proactive international response.
options.D: The European Union is solely responsible for the failure to protect citizens from recent natural disasters.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文從火災的嚴重性、氣候變遷的影響，到歐盟尋求新的應對策略（如購買專屬機隊），皆圍繞著「氣候變遷加劇了火災，迫使歐洲必須採取更積極的國際合作與防禦措施」這一主旨。選項 A 錯誤，文章強調的是氣候變遷而非人為疏失。選項 B 錯誤，文章提到許多地方火勢仍未受控，且消防員處境危險。選項 D 錯誤，文章並未指責歐盟為唯一責任方，而是強調歐盟正在努力改進應對機制。
